media.alt: AKU faculty attends WHO conference in Beirut on primary healthcare

content.text: As Primary Health Care is a major component of undergraduate medical education at The Aga Khan University (AKU), Dr Parvez Nayani, Senior Instructor, Department of Community Health Sciences, was invited to present the AKU experience at a recent conference in Beirut, organized by the World Health Organization (WHO) and the American University of Beirut.

The conference entitled, "Sustaining Primary Health Care in Academic Medicine as Basis to Training Doctors for the 21st Century: How to meet the Challenge," was attended by prominent medical academicians and WHO consultants from Geneva and Eastern Mediterranean Region. The participants analyzed the current situation in Primary Health Care teaching in different academic institutions, and developed approaches for strengthening it in the medical curricula.

A task group of four participants including Dr Nayani are preparing a detailed report on the conference deliberations. This report, expected within the next six weeks, will then be shared with national governments and medical colleges for implementation of its recommendations. Emphasis on teaching Primary Health Care would ensure that the trained physicians appropriately respond to the needs of their communities, rather than focusing only on tertiary care training.
